What needs you
Needs you lists what waits on you on every connected host. Activity is Rex\'s view of what programs are doing.
Everything a row can do
Long press a host, session or tab, or tap its ⋮: rename, move, new tab from a template, end.
A new session
+ starts a session. A session\'s New tab also runs your launch templates.
Settings
Notifications, the key bar, text size, the app lock and backup are here.
Help, any time
⋮ › Help and guide finds any feature and shows you where it is. It is in the terminal\'s ⋮ and the command palette too.
Add a host
⋮ › Add host, or Add host at the end of the list
A host is a computer running Rex. Give its address: over SSH (nothing to open on the computer), a tailnet, or the local network. Test connection checks each step before you save.
new computer server mac ssh address connect machine
Add a host from another computer
A link or QR code from the computer, or ⋮ › Import hosts

On the computer, tools/host-link.sh prints a rexpocket:// link and its QR code. Scan the code with the phone\'s camera, or open the link: Add host opens filled in for you to check. Import hosts takes a whole list, or a connected Rex\'s own list.
qr code scan camera link share import list desk laptop
See what needs you
The Needs you chip at the top of the home
Needs you lists every tab, on every connected host, whose program waits on you, failed or finished and was not seen. Working lists what is at work. The counts cover connected hosts only.
waiting blocked failed done attention filter running working
Rex\'s Activity view
The Activity chip: by priority or by session
Activity lists every tab a program reported on, as Rex\'s Activity view does: by priority (blocked, failed, done, working, idle) or by session. Include idle keeps idle tabs after you saw them.
activity priority session idle status programs
Find a host, session or tab
The search field at the bottom of the home
Type part of a name: the list narrows to the hosts, sessions and tabs that match, with every fold open. Back clears the search.
search filter look up find name
Start a session
+ at the bottom right of the home
+ makes a session on the connected host, or asks which host, and can connect one first. A session\'s ⋮ › New tab adds a tab to it.
new session create shell plus
Rename, move or end a session or tab
Long press the row, or tap its ⋮
Every host, session and tab has a sheet: rename, move up or down, new tab, mark as seen, status details, end or close. A tap opens or folds the row; it never connects.
rename move reorder end close kill delete long press menu sheet mark seen
Edit, move or remove a host
The host\'s ⋮ › Edit host, Move up, Remove host…
The host\'s sheet edits its address and name, moves it in the list, copies its address and removes it, with Undo.
edit change address port name remove delete order host
Run a command in a folder
New tab › Add template…: a name, a folder and a command

A launch template opens a tab that starts in a folder and runs a command, such as claude in ~/proj. Your templates are in every New tab: a session\'s, the host\'s and the terminal\'s ⋮, and the command palette.
template launch claude codex agent folder directory cwd command start run project
Silence a host
The host\'s ⋮ › Connection and notifications
A host\'s page turns its notifications off, or chooses which of its programs\' reports notify you, and whether it stays connected in the background. It also lists its muted tabs.
mute silence quiet notifications host background off
A Quick Settings tile
A host\'s or the tailnet\'s page › Add a tile

A tile in Android\'s Quick Settings connects or disconnects a host or the tailnet with one tap. Add it on the page, then drag it into the Quick Settings panel. The home screen widget lists what needs you.
tile quick settings shade widget shortcut launcher
Change the text size
⋮ › Text size, or pinch the terminal with two fingers

A pinch or − and + change this tab\'s size; the row shows the columns and rows it fits. Reset goes back to the default, which is in Settings › Appearance for every new tab. Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- work on a desk keyboard.
zoom font bigger smaller larger pinch scale columns wrap fit
Search every action
⋮ › Command palette, or Ctrl+Shift+P
The command palette lists everything the terminal can do, every tab of every session and your Rex actions, and finds them as you type. Help\'s entries are in it too.
command palette search actions everything keyboard ctrl shift p
Run your Rex actions
⋮ › Command palette: under their category
The actions in your Rex configuration (rex.action) are rows of the command palette, with their description, run for the pane on screen. A question an action asks shows as a dialog.
custom action rex lua config script category
Type a folder\'s or file\'s path
⋮ › Insert path, or the folder key on the key bar
Insert path browses the host\'s folders from where the program is, and types the folder or file you pick into the pane, quoted for the shell. Nothing runs until Return.
path folder directory file browse cd ls insert
Send a file to the host
⋮ › Send a file, or the attach key
Pick a file on the phone: it is uploaded to the host and its path typed into the pane, as dropping a file on a desk terminal does.
upload attach image photo file send share
Find in the output
⋮ › Find, or Ctrl+Shift+F
Find searches the pane\'s screen and scrollback, with each match marked, and moves between them.
find search scrollback output text match
Split a pane
⋮ › New pane on the right, or below
A new pane splits the tab, as on the desk. The phone shows one pane at a time: the dots over the key bar switch, and so does a sideways swipe.
split pane right below new pane divide
Switch tab, pane or session
Tap the title at the top of the terminal
The title opens the session\'s tabs and panes and the other sessions. The command palette finds a tab in any session by name.
switch tab pane session window navigate
Open a new tab
⋮ › New tab: a blank tab or a template
New tab offers a blank tab and your launch templates, and Add template… to make one. Ctrl+Shift+T opens a blank tab at once.
new tab window template blank
Copy or share all the output
⋮ › Copy output or Share output
Copy output takes the pane\'s screen and scrollback as text, each line as the program wrote it. Share output sends it to another app. Select text picks a part.
copy share output text clipboard log scrollback export
Full screen
⋮ › Full screen, or double tap the terminal
Full screen gives the pane the whole window. The corner button, the same gesture or Back leaves it.
full screen immersive hide bars bigger
Use a desk keyboard
⋮ › Keyboard shortcuts
With a keyboard on the desk, the screen\'s own shortcuts open the palette, Find, new tabs and the text size; Ctrl+Shift+/ lists them.
keyboard shortcuts hardware bluetooth desk keys
Approve, deny or reply to an agent
Needs you: Approve, Deny and Reply on the row
A row waiting on an agent\'s approval prompt has Approve and Deny, which send its keys without opening the pane; Reply sends a line, with your quick replies. A notification has the same buttons.
approve deny reply answer permission prompt yes no agent claude codex
Write a long prompt
⋮ › Compose prompt
The composer is a full editor for a prompt, sent in one paste with Return after it or not. Its draft stays with the pane until the program took it.
compose prompt editor message long paste draft write
Quick replies
Settings › Quick replies
Quick replies are what you tell agents most, one tap away in Reply, the composer, a notification and a key-bar panel. Edit, reorder or restore the defaults here.
quick reply canned snippet yes continue answer
Mute a tab
⋮ › Mute this tab, or Mute tab on its notification
A muted tab sends no notifications or progress bars. Expand a notification to find its Mute tab. Unmute in the same menu, or on the host\'s page, which lists its muted tabs.
mute silence quiet notification tab unmute
Pinch to zoom
Two fingers on the terminal: apart is bigger, together smaller
A pinch changes this tab\'s text size, so a wide table fits. ⋮ › Text size does the same with − and +.
pinch zoom gesture two fingers text size
Swipe to the next pane
Swipe sideways on the terminal
With two or more panes in a tab, a sideways swipe moves to the one beside it, as the dots over the key bar show. A drag up or down scrolls the history.
swipe gesture pane next previous scroll drag
Select text and open links
Long press the terminal; long press a link to open it
A long press selects, with handles to drag and Copy. On a link it offers Open, Copy and Share, whatever the long press is set to. ⋮ › Select text works too.
long press hold select copy link url open
Double tap
Double tap the terminal for full screen
By default a double tap enters full screen and a tap opens the keyboard. Settings › Terminal controls can change what each does.
double tap gesture full screen keyboard
A new line without sending
Hold the Return key on the key bar
Return held is Shift+Return: a new line in an agent\'s prompt instead of sending it. TalkBack offers it as an action of the key.
hold long press return enter new line shift multiline
Control chords
Tap Ctrl then a key, or hold Ctrl for the chords
Ctrl tapped applies to the next key, from the bar or the keyboard; tapped twice quickly it stays on. Held, it opens the chords: C-a to C-z in one more tap.
ctrl control chord hold modifier c-r c-d
Change what a tap does
Settings › Terminal controls › Tap, Double tap, Long press
Choose what a tap, a double tap and a long press do on the terminal, and how long each waits.
gesture tap double tap long press settings keyboard toggle
The folder key
The folder key on the key bar
It opens Insert path: a folder on the host, from where the program is, whose path - or a file\'s - is typed into the pane. Next to it, the attach key sends a file from the phone.
folder key insert path directory file attach paperclip
Add or remove keys
Settings › Terminal controls › Arrange keys
Put any key on the bar - F10, Home, PgDn, a letter, C-d - reorder or hide them, and make key groups from presets for htop, vim or tmux.
key bar keys arrange customize f1 f10 home end pgup esc fn htop vim tmux group
Notifications while the app is closed
Settings › Background and notifications › Background alerts
Background alerts keep hosts connected while the app is away, so a program waiting, failing or finishing notifies you, with Reply, Approve, Deny and Mute on the notification.
notification alert background push sound vibrate when done
Use a tailnet
Settings › Tailnet
The app can join your tailnet itself, such as Tailscale, so it reaches a computer at home without opening a port or running a VPN app. Its sheet lists the devices on it, each with Add host.
tailnet tailscale vpn wireguard mesh remote network
Lock the app
Settings › Security › Lock RexPocket
The app asks for your fingerprint, face or screen lock when you come back to it, at once or after a few minutes away. It asks you first when you turn it on.
lock biometric fingerprint face pin password security privacy
Block screenshots
Settings › Security › Block screenshots
Screenshots and screen recordings show nothing of the app, and its picture in recent apps is blank.
screenshot screen recording recents privacy secure
Back up settings
Settings › Export and import settings
Every setting, with your hosts and templates, goes to one file, encrypted with a passphrase when it holds keys, and back on another phone.
backup export import restore file move phone transfer
Dark or light
Settings › Appearance
The app\'s theme, the terminal\'s colours apart from it, the app\'s text size and the default terminal text size.
dark light theme night colours colors contrast text size
Terminal font
Settings › Terminal font
Pick the terminal\'s typeface - the phone\'s monospace or JetBrains Mono, downloaded once - and the default text size.
font typeface monospace nerd font ttf
Updates and previews
Settings › Updates
The app looks for a newer build once a day and offers it; nothing downloads until you say so. The channel above it chooses stable builds or previews.
update upgrade version preview stable channel install
Send a diagnostics report
Settings › Diagnostics
Diagnostics records what the app does and makes a report to share, with names, titles and messages left out.
diagnostics bug report log debug problem
